chunks: My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Ya'qub ibn Yazid said, on the authority of al-Ghifari, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Abd Allah (AS) that he said: The Messenger of Allah (SAWW) said:

Beware of arguing with every maniac, for every maniac has his proof dictated to him until the end of his term (death). When his term ends, his mischief will burn him in the Fire. It is also transmitted: 'His mistake troubles him and burns him.'

key_terms.مُفْتَنٍ: A maniac or one who is deluded/tested
key_terms.مُلْقَنُ حُجَّتِهِ: His proof is dictated to him

ai.seo_question: Why should one avoid debating with deluded people according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq includes this hadith in *Al-Tawhid* to illustrate the epistemological danger of engaging in speculative theology (*kalam*) with the deluded, whose arguments are divinely 'dictated' as a test until their appointed term ends. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between genuine knowledge and the deceptive rhetoric of those consumed by their own errors, which ultimately consume them in the Hereafter.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 25. My father (RA) said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said: Ya`qub ibn Yazid said, on the authority of alGhifari, on the authority of Ja`far ibn Ibrahim, that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (a.s) said: The Messenger of Allah (s.w) said: “

Beware of arguing wit every maniac. Verily, every maniac dictates his proof till the end of his time (death). When his life cameos to an end, his mischief will cause him to burn in the fire.” It is also transmitted, `his mistakes trouble him and burn him.’
